## SPAM Data Analysis

Soil Plant Assisted Migration (SPAM) data analysis using Subproject 4 data from previous year's (2025) data collection. Data from Subproject 4 was collected to understand the success of microbial dust spread among California native plants within Crystal Cove State Park.

## Loading Packages

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
install.packages("ggpubr")
install.packages("ggsignif")
```

## Importing Data

```{r}
SubProject4 <- 
  read_excel("Copy of SPAM SubProject 4 Inoculated Seeded Plots (1).xlsx", 
             sheet = "PlantDensity1")
```

## Summary Table

```{r}
#include measures of center and variability, sample sizes, and statistical test results 

summary <- SubProject4 |> 
  group_by(Plot,`Species Code`,`Spp Count`, `Spp Height`) |> 
  summarize(mean_height = mean(`Spp Height`, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_height = sd(`Spp Height`, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(),
            se_height = sd_height/sqrt(n))

summary
```

## Exploratory Data Analysis

```{r}
#time to make graphs and check out what data looks like

view(SubProject4)

ggplot(SubProject4) +
  aes(x = `Species Code`, y = `Spp Height`, color = Plot) +
  geom_boxplot()
#wow a colorful mess. 
    
ggplot(SubProject4) +
  aes(y = `Spp Height`) +
  geom_histogram()+
  facet_grid(~`Species Code`)
#still a mess

ggplot(SubProject4) +
  aes(x = Plot, y = `Spp Height`) +
  geom_jitter()
#a little better? I can hardly even read the plot names. is there is a way to work around so much data that was collect. 
```

## ANOVA Analysis

```{r}
#1 anova analysis that includes both treatment variables and blocking on the response variable 
#test of assumptions should be fully described
#results of tests with interactions should be reported in ANOVA table 
#graph
#normality test


model  <- lm(`Spp Height` ~ `Species Code` + Plot, data = SubProject4)
plot(model)
ggpubr::ggqqplot(residuals(model))
#test of normality
#Subproject 4 data does not look normal from the residuals vs fitted graph. The residuals vs fitted graph shows heterscadisity. The qq plot does not show normal data.



SubProject4 %>% rstatix::levene_test(`Spp Height` ~ `Species Code` * Plot)
#levene's test/test of variance. 
#note to self: this doesn't work? but why?


```

```{r}

model_aov<- aov(`Spp Height` ~ `Species Code` + Plot, SubProject4)
summary(model_aov)
#statistical test
#The summary table shows that species code has a significant effect on plant height(p value 5.86e-11). Plot has a significant effect of plant height (p value 0.0342) but not as strong as species code. This makes sense, each species has a differnt average growth height. 


TukeyHSD(model_aov)
#note to self: this doesn't work. what? why?
```

```{r}
summary_stats <- SubProject4 |> 
  group_by(Plot, `Species Code`) |> 
  summarize(mean_height = mean(`Spp Height`, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_height = sd(`Spp Height`, na.rm = TRUE),
            n = n(),
            se_height = sd_height/sqrt(n))
summary_stats
#summary stat table. 
#note to self:not helpful, consider grouping by plot number, plot treatment, invasive or native species.


ggplot(summary_stats) + 
  aes(x = Plot, y = mean_height, fill = `Species Code`) + 
  geom_col() + 
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = mean_height - se_height, ymax = mean_height + se_height), width = 0.2)
#figures
#Graph makes sense because an ARTCAL would definitely be larger than a phacelia species.
#note to self: consider grouping or removing soem of the species code or the plot. 
```

## Regression Analysis

```{r}
model_lm <- lm(`Spp Height` ~ `Species Code` + Plot, SubProject4) 
plot(model_lm)
summary(model_lm)
#normality test
#From the Residuals vs Fitted graph, it does not show homoscedasticity. The spread is not the same across the horizontal line on the graph. The qq plot also shows the data is not normal. 


ggplot(SubProject4)+
  aes((`Species Code`), log(`Spp Height`))+
  geom_col()
#lets tranform
#note to self: gosh this isn't helpful. how and why are some of the values below 0?
```

model_lm <- lm(`Spp Height` ~ `Species Code` + Plot, SubProject4) 
summary(model_lm)
